title: Connection
note: The main status screen uses existing client data. It does not imply protection for all internet traffic. Duration and counters are samples.

title: Disconnected
note: The connection uses one current configuration. If system permission has already been granted, the button goes straight to connection progress.

title: Welcome
note: A new mobile entry point to the existing wizard. No account registration or public VPN server directory.

title: VPN permission
note: A system-owned permission prompt before connecting, when required. Android supplies the exact wording and appearance. This design only illustrates the dialog.
source: Android Developers: VPN, User experience / Prepare a service

title: Connecting
note: The four checks match the desktop client directly. Success transitions to the connected state automatically. In the mockup, choose the outcome from the scenario selector.

title: Reconnecting
note: Reconnecting is distinct from connected. Recovery does not promise network availability or blocking of traffic outside the VPN.

title: Connection error
note: HTTP details are offered only when the client has actually captured them. Input errors and transport errors must remain distinct.

title: Disconnecting
note: Waiting for confirmation matches the desktop behavior. A timeout must never be presented as success.

title: Status unavailable
note: The mobile equivalent of unavailable service status. A new status read may return any confirmed state. The link to connecting is just a sample path.

title: Background notification
note: A replacement for the desktop tray icon. The system supplies the actual notification template. This is not a working Android notification.

title: Settings
note: This hub preserves every desktop menu item. AutoConnect, TLS and runtime limits remain accessible through the complete JSON editor.

title: Before setup
note: The existing disconnectGate. The first step starts only after disconnection is confirmed. A client that is already disconnected skips this screen.

title: Server address
note: The first of the four original steps. Verify only changes the screen in this mockup. It does not contact the server.

title: HTTP headers
note: An adaptation of the separate HTTP headers editor. Text is neither carried between pages nor saved in the mockup.

title: Server secret
note: Both custom and default secrets are retained. The mobile design hides sensitive input by default and allows it to be revealed temporarily.

title: IP and access key
note: Automatic IP suggestions and a default access key already exist in the client. If no address is suggested, the user can enter one manually.

title: Complete setup
note: The counts illustrate a /24 network with 252 possible remote clients. Defaults are added only on Finish. This option is disabled for unsupported configurations.

title: Configuration saved
note: A confirmed save is a separate state. Connecting is an explicit choice. Saving does not start the VPN automatically.

title: Verification error
note: A crypto_tag_mismatch error variant. A timeout does not invalidate the inputs. The real error message must not repeat the secret.

title: Communication contracts
note: The wide desktop table becomes a list with detail screens. All candidate addresses remain paginated. The local IP is excluded from the targets.

title: Contract details
note: The key is hidden by default on mobile. In the implementation, the key of a disabled contract is read-only. The sample switch only changes its visual state.

title: Key from password
note: Password, SHA-256, Default and Random are retained. This mockup deliberately does not implement cryptography or password generation.

title: Invalid key
note: The error belongs to a specific contract and field. The list retains the other unsaved changes.

title: Configuration editor
note: The complete JSON editor also covers parameters without a dedicated desktop form. Sample values are not a recommended production configuration. Android storage is private to the app and does not reuse the Windows path.

title: Reset configuration
note: Reset changes the draft document. It is not presented as an immediate write to the saved configuration.

title: Changes saved
note: The desktop already offers reconnect after saving. The implementation must complete disconnection before starting a new connection. If the VPN is inactive, offer Connect instead.

title: Traffic statistics
note: All ten statistics fields are retained. No invented speed, ping, monthly history or chart based on unsupported data.

title: Last known statistics
note: The stale state retains the last counters and clearly marks them as out of date. Dashes appear before the first values arrive.

title: Who is online
note: Online with a valid contract, online with an invalid contract and offline states are retained. The summary counts online clients and valid contracts. The local client is omitted. Longer lists use pagination.

title: Server data
note: A readable view of the complete JSON without renaming fields. The sample serverVersion is not a released version. This is a separate diagnostic sample, not the source for the list on the previous screen.

title: HTTP response
note: The Request and Response tabs are retained, including notices about incomplete or reconstructed data.

title: HTTP request
note: Labeling the data source prevents a reconstruction from being mistaken for a complete network capture.

title: Unsaved changes
note: A shared pattern for system Back and closing the wizard, editor or contracts. In production, returning restores the original form. This example uses the wizard.

title: Save result unknown
note: Distinguishes the wizard commitUnknown state from the contracts unknown state. The wizard checks a receipt, while contracts read the current configuration. Retrying a write is offered only after the result has been evaluated.

title: About
note: About remains available. The design does not invent a current version number or unsupported licensing information.

title: Closing the app
note: An adaptation of desktop Exit. The mobile UI should not pretend to force-stop the process. Leaving an activity and stopping the VPN are separate actions.

title: Configuration needs attention
note: Covers missing, invalid and unreadable configurations. Editing must depend on whether the document is actually readable. A missing identity leads to the wizard.

title: VPN permission denied
note: An Android addition to the existing connection flow. Denying permission is not a server error.
source: Android Developers: VPN, Prepare a service

title: Disconnection unconfirmed
note: Matches Disconnect not confirmed. No false confirmation on timeout.

title: JSON error
note: An example of a syntax error. The actual wording must come from the validator. Do not promise an exact line number unless the validator provides it.

title: Reset wizard
note: A separate wizard reset variant. The mockup keeps a sample URL filled in. The actual reset uses the default placeholder.

title: More contracts
note: Pagination retains draft values by target IP, not just for the visible rows.

title: Default editor content
note: A reset preview without overwriting the actual configuration. The service would supply the complete default document.

title: Loading statistics
note: Missing data is not zero. This matches the waiting for service status state.

title: No server records
note: A valid response with an empty list, distinct from a loading failure.

title: Server refresh failed
note: The last successful response is retained on error. Without previous data, show only an explanation and an option to retry.

title: Save checked
note: One outcome after Check current configuration. A confirmed write shows success instead of a retry. A conflict must never cause a silent overwrite.

title: Wizard session expired
note: The existing sessionExpired state. An outdated verification result must not be used to save a new configuration.

title: Connection checks
note: A separate view of successful checks. Opening it never starts a new connection.
